Class StorageAttachment<O,C>

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.core.StorageAttachment<O,C>
Type Parameters:
O - owner type (Void for ephemeral, Player / BlockEntity / etc. for persistent variants)
C - content type — NonNullList of ItemStack for most v1 factories; ItemContainerContents for itemContainer(int); consumer-defined for custom specs
Direct Known Subclasses:
StorageAttachment.PlayerStorageAttachment
public abstract class StorageAttachment<O,C> extends Object
M7 — Storage Attachment Taxonomy. Public entry point for slot-group content persistence, by owner type.

Produces a Storage bound to a specific owner instance. The returned Storage reads/writes whatever persistence surface the factory declared — Fabric attachment (Player, BlockEntity), data component (ItemStack), in-memory list (Ephemeral), or consumer-supplied hooks (CustomAttachmentSpec).

See Design Docs/Mechanisms/M7_STORAGE_ATTACHMENT.md for design rationale including the per-entry Principle 11 check that scoped v1 to four factories (ephemeral, playerAttached, blockScoped, itemContainer) + custom extension. Block-portable and entity-attached are deferred to first-concrete-consumer trigger.

Usage

// At mod init — declare the attachment.
public static final StorageAttachment<BlockEntity, NonNullList<ItemStack>> FURNACE_EXTRA =
    StorageAttachment.blockScoped("my-mod", "furnace_extra", 1);

// At menu construction — bind to a specific owner instance.
Storage storage = FURNACE_EXTRA.bind(furnaceBE);
panel.slotGroup("extra").slot(0, 0).build(storage);

    • slotCount

      public abstract int slotCount()

    • bind

      public abstract Storage bind(O owner)
      Binds this attachment to a specific owner instance. Returns a Storage view that reads/writes the attachment's content for that owner.

      For owners with stable references during the menu lifetime (Player, BlockEntity, Entity), pass the reference directly.

    • bind

      public Storage bind(Supplier<O> ownerSupplier)
      Binds via a live supplier for owners whose reference can change during the menu lifetime (notably ItemStack, which vanilla may replace during interactions). The library calls the supplier on every read/write.

    • ephemeral

      public static StorageAttachment<Void, net.minecraft.core.NonNullList<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack>> ephemeral(int slotCount)
      Session-scoped, in-memory storage. Content dies when the menu closes unless the handler's close-drop policy captures it. Equivalent to wrapping an EphemeralStorage — StorageAttachment presents it through the unified API.

      Owner type is Void; callers pass null to bind(O).

    • playerAttached

      public static StorageAttachment.PlayerStorageAttachment<net.minecraft.core.NonNullList<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack>> playerAttached(String namespace, String path, int slotCount)
      Persists slot-group content on a Player via a Fabric attachment. Content travels with the player across sessions and dimensions.

      Death handling

      Player content attachments are enrolled in death handling at DropRule.DEFAULT — zero-config vanilla parity: on death the content drops at the death spot when keepInventory is off (Curse of Vanishing destroys instead) and is kept across respawn when keepInventory is on. Override per attachment with dropsOnDeath(DropRule) — e.g. KEEP for a soulbound slot. (The attachment registers copyOnDeath so the kept path carries across respawn; the library owns the gamerule-gated drop.)
      Parameters:
      namespace - attachment-id namespace (consumer's mod id)
      path - attachment-id path (unique per consumer-declared attachment)
      slotCount - number of item slots the content holds

    • blockScoped

      public static StorageAttachment<net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity, net.minecraft.core.NonNullList<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack>> blockScoped(String namespace, String path, int slotCount)
      Persists slot-group content on a BlockEntity via a Fabric attachment. Content dies with the block — breaking destroys the attachment. Intended for dies-with-block containers (chest, furnace, hopper, etc.).
      Parameters:
      namespace - attachment-id namespace (consumer's mod id)
      path - attachment-id path (unique per consumer-declared attachment)
      slotCount - number of item slots the content holds

    • entityAttached

      public static StorageAttachment<net.minecraft.world.entity.Entity, net.minecraft.core.NonNullList<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack>> entityAttached(String namespace, String path, int slotCount)
      Persists slot-group content on a generic Entity via a Fabric attachment. Content saves with the entity in its NBT and dies with it — no respawn carry (unlike playerAttached(String, String, int), which has death handling; an entity is not a player). For entity-owned containers (minecart with chest, donkey/llama/mule, future entity-scoped slots).

      Server-persistent; the client view is kept current by the menu's vanilla slot protocol (the registered slots write the client-side attachment on each ContainerSetSlot), the same way playerAttached(String, String, int) content displays without a separate attachment sync.

      Parameters:
      namespace - attachment-id namespace (consumer's mod id)
      path - attachment-id path (unique per consumer-declared attachment)
      slotCount - number of item slots the content holds

    • itemContainer

      public static StorageAttachment<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack, net.minecraft.world.item.component.ItemContainerContents> itemContainer(int slotCount)
      Persists slot-group content on an ItemStack via vanilla's DataComponents.CONTAINER component (ItemContainerContents). Content travels with the item through menus, pickup, drop, throw.

      v1 hardcodes DataComponents.CONTAINER as the component type — the canonical vanilla surface for item-backed slot groups (shulker items, bundles). A fully-generic itemAttached(DataComponentType<C>, ...) factory is a follow-on when a concrete consumer surfaces needing a non-CONTAINER component.

      Because ItemStacks can be replaced by vanilla during interactions (e.g., when a slot is vacated), prefer bind(Supplier) over bind(Object) for item-backed storage.

    • custom

      public static <O,C> StorageAttachment<O,C> custom(CustomAttachmentSpec<O,C> spec)
      Wraps a CustomAttachmentSpec as a StorageAttachment. Used for owner types outside the four v1 factories AND as the decorator-path escape hatch for consumers whose save/load doesn't route through a MenuKit handler.

      This is the NON-player path: the returned base StorageAttachment has no dropsOnDeath (death handling is player-only). For a player-anchored custom spec that needs death handling, use customPlayerAttached(CustomAttachmentSpec) — it returns a StorageAttachment.PlayerStorageAttachment so dropsOnDeath is reachable.

      Type Parameters:
      O - owner type
      C - content type

    • customPlayerAttached

      public static <C> StorageAttachment.PlayerStorageAttachment<C> customPlayerAttached(CustomAttachmentSpec<net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player, C> spec)
      Wraps a player-anchored CustomAttachmentSpec as a StorageAttachment.PlayerStorageAttachment, so it can opt into death handling via StorageAttachment.PlayerStorageAttachment.dropsOnDeath(DropRule) (§0052). The spec's owner type MUST be Player; that is what the typed factory asserts statically (unlike the old base dropsOnDeath, which threw at runtime on a non-player spec).

      The library owns the gamerule-gated DROP/DESTROY at the death site; KEEP-across-respawn is the consumer storage's own responsibility — set copyOnDeath on your Fabric attachment (or use a persistent store). The library cannot set copyOnDeath on storage it does not own (the whole point of a custom spec).

      Type Parameters:
      C - content type
